challenges.headline: One invoice per signed contract
challenges.premise: The request treats 'create an invoice' as a single document produced once, at signature.
challenges.alternative: Modeling the contract-to-invoice relationship as one-to-many from the start — supporting milestone, recurring or partial billing schedules — avoids rebuilding the trigger later when a subscription or phased contract shows up.
challenges.consequence: If billing is actually milestone-based or recurring for some contracts, a single-invoice trigger will need to be re-architected into a schedule engine, and any invoices already issued under the wrong model complicate the migration.
challenges.recommendation: Confirm with Finance whether any current or near-term contracts bill in installments or on a recurring basis before scoping this as a single-document trigger.

challenges.headline: Auto-issuing at signature
challenges.premise: The invoice is expected to exist, fully formed, the moment the contract is signed — implying it could be issued immediately.
challenges.alternative: Creating the invoice in a draft state at signature, with a finance validation step before it moves to issued, keeps a legally-numbered, VAT-bearing document from being generated with wrong or incomplete data.
challenges.consequence: French invoice numbering is sequential and largely irreversible — an auto-issued invoice with the wrong amount or missing VAT can't simply be edited, only corrected via credit note, which is exactly the kind of error this automation was meant to prevent.
challenges.recommendation: Decide with Finance whether the automation should produce a draft awaiting validation, or an issued document, before building the numbering/issuance path.

challenges.headline: One global rule vs per-client config
challenges.premise: The trigger and billing logic are described as if they apply uniformly, with no mention of variation by client or contract type.
challenges.alternative: Given this is a configurable multi-client platform where billing rules commonly differ by client/contract/country, treating the trigger and amount-derivation logic as configurable from day one avoids retrofitting a rule engine after client-specific exceptions surface.
challenges.consequence: Building this as a hardcoded trigger first means the first client needing a different billing schedule or VAT treatment forces a rework of the core mechanism, not just a config addition.
challenges.recommendation: Ask whether any known client or contract type already needs different billing timing or rules before finalizing the design as global.

idempotency and retry handling on an event-driven trigger
legal numbering and VAT compliance leaving little room for post-issuance correction
briefs.cost_driver: the billing-rule derivation and invoice-generation logic sitting between the contract-signed event and a compliant invoice
risks: Legal invoice numbering rules mean a duplicate or premature invoice can't be silently deleted — only corrected via credit note, which is a compliance-visible event.
No idempotency definition yet for the contract-signed event, and duplicate processing is a realistic failure mode in event-driven systems.
Permissions on the resulting invoice are undefined; without a review gate, an incomplete or wrong invoice could reach a client-facing role before validation.
If billing is later found to be one-to-many (milestones/recurring), the initial single-document model will need a non-trivial rework, not a patch.
Contract data may be incomplete at signature time (missing VAT rate, billing contact) with no defined fallback (block, draft, fail) yet agreed.

opportunities.text: Build the contract-signed subscriber as a generic 'trigger on lifecycle event' mechanism reusable for mission end-of-mission invoicing and other downstream automations.
If milestone/recurring billing is confirmed, the billing-schedule engine built here can become the standard mechanism for all contract-derived billing, not a one-off.
An audit trail on auto-generated invoices (who/what triggered creation, what data it derived) could feed directly into financial reporting's reconciliation and audit needs.

next_steps: Confirm with Finance whether a signed contract produces exactly one invoice or a billing schedule (milestones/recurring/partial) before estimating.
Decide the invoice's initial state at creation — draft pending validation, or issued — given the irreversibility of legal numbering.
Define the expected behavior when the same signature event is processed twice, and when contract billing data is incomplete at signing.
Clarify whether the trigger and billing rules must be configurable per client/contract/country before locking the design as global.

challenges.headline: One invoice per signed contract
challenges.premise: The request assumes a signed contract produces exactly one invoice for its full amount.
challenges.alternative: Model invoicing as a schedule generated from the contract's billing terms (milestone, recurring, or partial), with signature only initiating that schedule rather than emitting a single document.
challenges.consequence: Building a one-shot generator now means re-architecting the trigger and data model later if any contract needs milestone or recurring billing — and the platform's own contract/invoice relationship is explicitly one-to-many.
challenges.recommendation: Confirm with Finance/Sales whether any contract type requires more than one invoice before locking the trigger shape.

challenges.headline: Signature blocks invoice creation
challenges.premise: The workflow implicitly treats invoice creation as an inline, synchronous step at the moment of signature.
challenges.alternative: Treat signature as firing an asynchronous, queued event that creates the invoice in a visible 'pending' state, so a failure in invoice generation (missing VAT data, incomplete contract) never blocks or breaks the signature flow itself.
challenges.consequence: A synchronous design means any invoice-generation failure — bad amount source, missing tax data — surfaces as a broken signature action in front of the client-facing user, and retries risk duplicate invoices.
challenges.recommendation: Decide sync-vs-async explicitly with engineering before estimating; design the duplicate-guard around whichever is chosen.

challenges.headline: Invoice goes out unreviewed
challenges.premise: The request implies the invoice is simply 'created,' without saying whether it is issued immediately or held for finance review.
challenges.alternative: Create the invoice in draft status, visible only to finance/admin roles, with an explicit validation step before it is issued and sent to the client.
challenges.consequence: Skipping review risks a wrong amount, VAT error, or premature document reaching the client under legal numbering rules that are hard to reverse once issued.
challenges.recommendation: Confirm the required approval step and who holds edit/view rights on the auto-created invoice before build.

challenges.headline: One invoice per signed contract
challenges.premise: The request implies a single invoice is created the moment a contract is signed.

challenges.headline: Signature-triggered issuance, not draft
challenges.premise: The request reads as if the invoice should exist and presumably be usable right after signature, with no review step described.
challenges.alternative: Create the invoice in draft state on signature, with an explicit review/approval step before it is issued and gets a legal invoice number.
challenges.consequence: An invoice issued automatically at the moment of signing, with no review, risks going out with wrong amounts or VAT before anyone checks it — and once issued, French numbering rules make it a legal document that can't just be edited or deleted.
challenges.recommendation: Validate the required approval step and who owns it before the invoice becomes 'issued', not after.

challenges.headline: Signature event assumed synchronous
challenges.premise: The trigger is described as immediate ('when signed, created automatically'), without saying whether this is inline/blocking or queued/eventual.
challenges.alternative: Treat contract signature as an asynchronous event the invoicing flow subscribes to, with a visible pending state and retry/ordering handling, rather than a synchronous call inside the signing action.
challenges.consequence: A synchronous design means a failure in invoice creation can block or fail the contract-signing action itself, coupling two lifecycles that should be independent.
challenges.recommendation: Decide sync vs. async with the team that owns the contract signature flow before implementation starts.
